# Phase 3: Development

**Version:** 1.0  
**Last Updated:** 2026-02-09  
**Phase Number:** 3 of 7

## Duration Estimates by Project Type

| Project Type | Duration | Complexity |
|-------------|----------|------------|
| POC | 3-7 days | Low-Medium |
| Prototype | 7-14 days | Medium |
| MVP | 14-30 days | High |
| Handover | 21-45 days | Very High |

## Description

Phase 3 is where designs become reality. Development teams implement features according to approved specifications, following coding standards and best practices. This phase emphasizes incremental development, continuous integration, code quality, and iterative delivery.

## Objectives

- ✓ Implement all features per design specifications
- ✓ Write clean, maintainable, well-documented code
- ✓ Achieve required unit test coverage
- ✓ Follow coding standards and best practices
- ✓ Conduct thorough code reviews
- ✓ Integrate code continuously (CI/CD)
- ✓ Track and resolve defects promptly
- ✓ Deliver working software incrementally

---

## 1. Phase Overview

### Purpose
Transform approved designs into functional, tested, production-ready code. Implement features incrementally, ensuring quality through continuous testing, code reviews, and integration.

### Goals
1. **Feature Implementation:** Build all required features per PRD and design specs
2. **Code Quality:** Maintain high code quality through reviews and standards
3. **Test Coverage:** Achieve target test coverage (85-95% based on project type)
4. **Integration:** Continuously integrate code with automated testing
5. **Documentation:** Document code, APIs, and implementation decisions
6. **Velocity:** Maintain consistent development velocity
7. **Defect Management:** Identify and fix defects early

### Success Criteria
- ✓ All features implemented per acceptance criteria
- ✓ Unit test coverage meets targets (POC: 85%, Prototype: 90%, MVP/Handover: 95%)
- ✓ All code reviewed and approved (100% review coverage)
- ✓ CI/CD pipeline operational
- ✓ No critical or high-priority bugs in code
- ✓ Code quality metrics met (maintainability index, complexity)
- ✓ Technical debt documented and minimized
- ✓ API documentation generated and accurate

---

## 2. Prerequisites

### From Phase 2 (Design)
- ✓ Approved architecture documentation
- ✓ Database schema with DDL scripts
- ✓ API specifications (OpenAPI format)
- ✓ UI/UX designs and specifications
- ✓ Design system (for user-facing features)
- ✓ Technology stack selected
- ✓ Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

### Technical Prerequisites
- ✓ Development environments set up
- ✓ Version control repository initialized
- ✓ CI/CD pipeline configured
- ✓ Code quality tools configured (linters, formatters)
- ✓ Test frameworks set up
- ✓ Database instances available (dev, test)
- ✓ Development tools and licenses available
- ✓ Access to APIs and third-party services

### Resource Prerequisites
- ✓ Development team assembled (Backend, Frontend, Full-Stack)
- ✓ Team members have necessary access and permissions
- ✓ Development workstations configured
- ✓ Communication channels established
- ✓ Sprint/iteration planning completed

## 4. Deliverables

| Deliverable | Owner | Format | Location |
|------------|-------|--------|----------|
| Application Source Code | Dev Team | Code files | `src/` |
| Unit Tests | Dev Team | Test files | `tests/unit/` |
| Integration Tests | Dev Team | Test files | `tests/integration/` |

### Project Type Specific Deliverables

#### POC Projects
- Core feature implementations (minimal)
- Basic unit tests (85% coverage)

#### Prototype Projects

#### MVP Projects

- Comprehensive test suite (95% coverage)

- Component library documentation
- Deployment documentation
- Code quality reports
- Performance benchmarks

#### Handover Projects
- Complete feature set with polish
- Comprehensive test coverage (95%+)
- Complete API documentation with examples
- Developer onboarding guide
- Architecture documentation updates
- Code quality and security reports
- Performance optimization documentation
- Troubleshooting guide

### Optional Deliverables
- E2E tests (recommended for MVP/Handover)

- Load test results
- Security scan reports
- Code coverage reports

## 5. Sub-Phases

### Sub-Phase 3.1: Development Environment Setup (Days 1-2)

**Activities:**
- Set up local development environments
- Clone repository and configure tools
- Install dependencies
- Configure database instances
- Set up CI/CD pipeline
- Configure linters and formatters
- Set up testing frameworks
- Verify all tools working

**Outputs:**
- Development environments ready
- CI/CD pipeline operational
- All developers can build and run project
- Development standards document

**Duration by Type:**
- POC: 0.5 day
- Prototype: 1 day
- MVP: 1-2 days
- Handover: 2-3 days

### Sub-Phase 3.2: Sprint 1 - Foundation (Days 2-8)

**Activities:**
- Set up project structure
- Implement database migrations
- Create base classes/modules
- Implement authentication/authorization
- Set up API framework
- Create UI component library foundation
- Implement core utilities
- Write foundation tests

**Outputs:**
- Project scaffolding complete
- Database schema implemented
- Authentication working
- Base API structure ready
- UI component foundations
- Foundation test suite

**Duration by Type:**
- POC: 1-2 days
- Prototype: 2-4 days
- MVP: 3-6 days
- Handover: 4-8 days

### Sub-Phase 3.3: Sprint 2+ - Feature Development (Days 7-30+)

**Activities:**
- Implement features per priority
- Write unit tests for each feature
- Conduct code reviews
- Fix defects
- Integrate features
- Update documentation
- Refactor as needed
- Run integration tests

**Outputs:**
- Implemented features
- Feature test suites
- Code review approvals
- Updated documentation

**Duration by Type:**
- POC: 2-4 days
- Prototype: 4-8 days
- MVP: 10-20 days
- Handover: 15-30 days

**Note:** This sub-phase repeats in iterations/sprints until all features complete

### Sub-Phase 3.4: Integration & Refinement (Days 25-35)

**Activities:**
- Integrate all features
- Conduct end-to-end testing
- Performance optimization
- Security hardening
- Code refactoring
- Technical debt remediation
- Documentation completion
- Final code reviews

**Outputs:**
- Fully integrated application
- Optimized code
- Complete test suite
- Final documentation

**Duration by Type:**
- POC: 0.5-1 day
- Prototype: 1-2 days
- MVP: 3-5 days
- Handover: 4-7 days

### Sub-Phase 3.5: Code Freeze & Handover (Days 30-40)

**Activities:**
- Code freeze
- Final testing
- Documentation review
- Deployment preparation
- Knowledge transfer sessions
- Create deployment artifacts
- Final code quality checks

**Outputs:**
- Production-ready code
- Complete documentation
- Deployment packages
- Handover report

**Duration by Type:**
- POC: 0.5 day
- Prototype: 1 day
- MVP: 2-3 days
- Handover: 3-5 days

## 7. Quality Gates

### Entry Criteria

Before starting Phase 3:
- ✓ Phase 2 exit criteria met
- ✓ Architecture and design approved
- ✓ Development environments ready
- ✓ Development team onboarded
- ✓ CI/CD pipeline configured
- ✓ Development standards defined
- ✓ Sprint/iteration plan created

### In-Progress Checkpoints

#### Checkpoint 1: Foundation Complete (End of Sub-Phase 3.2)
**Criteria:**
- ✓ Project structure established
- ✓ Database schema implemented
- ✓ Authentication working
- ✓ CI/CD pipeline running
- ✓ First features implemented
- ✓ Initial tests passing

**Actions if Not Met:**
- Review and fix foundation issues
- Adjust timeline if needed
- Escalate blockers

#### Checkpoint 2: Mid-Development Review (50% features complete)
**Criteria:**
- ✓ 50% of features implemented
- ✓ Test coverage tracking to target
- ✓ Code review compliance high
- ✓ No critical defects outstanding
- ✓ Velocity stable

**Actions if Not Met:**
- Adjust scope or timeline
- Increase code review rigor
- Address technical debt
- Add resources if needed

#### Checkpoint 3: Feature Complete (End of Sub-Phase 3.3)
**Criteria:**
- ✓ All features implemented
- ✓ All feature tests passing
- ✓ Integration tests passing
- ✓ Code reviews complete
- ✓ Documentation updated

**Actions if Not Met:**
- Extend development timeline
- Prioritize remaining features
- Defer low-priority items

### Exit Criteria

Phase 3 is complete when ALL criteria met:

#### Feature Completeness
- ✓ All required features implemented per PRD
- ✓ All acceptance criteria met
- ✓ All features integrated and working together
- ✓ No critical or high-priority bugs

#### Code Quality
- ✓ All code reviewed and approved (100% review coverage)
- ✓ Code quality metrics met (complexity, maintainability)
- ✓ Coding standards followed
- ✓ No critical code smells
- ✓ Technical debt documented

#### Test Coverage
- ✓ Unit test coverage meets target:
  - POC: ≥85%
  - Prototype: ≥90%
  - MVP: ≥95%
  - Handover: ≥95%
- ✓ Integration tests complete and passing
- ✓ All tests passing in CI/CD pipeline
- ✓ Test quality verified (meaningful tests, not just coverage)

#### Documentation
- ✓ Code comments sufficient
- ✓ API documentation complete and accurate
- ✓ README with setup instructions
- ✓ Component documentation complete
- ✓ Architecture updates documented

#### CI/CD
- ✓ All commits build successfully
- ✓ All automated tests passing
- ✓ Code quality checks passing
- ✓ Deployment artifacts generated

#### Approvals
- ✓ Technical Architect approval
- ✓ Product Manager acceptance of features
- ✓ Security review passed (if required)
- ✓ Go/No-Go decision for Phase 4

## 8. Testing Requirements

### Unit Testing

**Requirements:**
- Every public function/method tested
- Edge cases covered
- Error handling tested
- Mocking/stubbing for dependencies
- Fast execution (<10ms per test average)

**Coverage Targets:**
- POC: 85%
- Prototype: 90%
- MVP: 95%
- Handover: 95%

**Tools:**
- Backend: JUnit, pytest, Mocha (language-specific)
- Frontend: Jest, React Testing Library, Vitest

### Integration Testing

**Requirements:**
- API endpoint testing (all endpoints)
- Database integration testing
- Third-party service integration testing
- Component integration testing (frontend)

**Coverage:**
- All critical user paths
- All API endpoints
- All database operations
- All third-party integrations

### Code Quality Testing

**Tools & Metrics:**
- Linting: ESLint, Pylint, RuboCop
- Formatting: Prettier, Black, gofmt
- Complexity: SonarQube, CodeClimate
- Security: Snyk, Bandit, npm audit

**Thresholds:**
- No critical linting errors
- Cyclomatic complexity <15
- Maintainability index >65
- No critical security vulnerabilities

### Continuous Testing

- All tests run on every commit
- Test results visible in CI/CD
- Failed tests block merges
- Test execution time monitored

---

## 9. Documentation Requirements

### Code Documentation

**Requirements:**
- All public APIs documented
- Complex logic explained with comments
- Non-obvious decisions documented
- TODOs tracked and linked to issues

**Standards:**
- Use language-specific documentation standards (JSDoc, docstrings, etc.)
- Include examples for complex functions
- Document parameters, return values, exceptions

### API Documentation

**Location:** `docs/api/`  
**Format:** OpenAPI/Swagger (auto-generated from code)

**Contents:**
- All endpoints documented
- Request/response examples
- Authentication requirements
- Error responses
- Rate limiting information

### README Documentation

**Location:** `README.md`

**Contents:**
- Project overview
- Prerequisites
- Installation instructions
- Configuration guide
- Running the application
- Running tests
- Common issues and troubleshooting
- Contributing guidelines
- License information

### Component Documentation

**Location:** `docs/components/` (frontend)

**Contents:**
- Component purpose
- Props/inputs documentation
- Usage examples
- Accessibility notes
- Browser compatibility

### Database Documentation

**Location:** `docs/database/`

**Contents:**
- Schema diagrams (updated if changed)
- Migration history
- Seeding data instructions
- Common queries

## 12. Risk Management

### Common Risks in Phase 3

#### Risk 1: Scope Creep
**Probability:** High  
**Impact:** High  
**Mitigation:**
- Strict change control process
- Product Manager gates all scope changes
- Document all changes with impact analysis
- Defer non-critical features to backlog

#### Risk 2: Low Code Quality
**Probability:** Medium  
**Impact:** High  
**Mitigation:**
- Mandatory code reviews (100% coverage)
- Automated code quality gates
- Regular refactoring time
- Pair programming for complex features

#### Risk 3: Insufficient Test Coverage
**Probability:** Medium  
**Impact:** High  
**Mitigation:**
- Test coverage tracking from day 1
- TDD/BDD practices encouraged
- Test coverage gates in CI/CD
- Regular test review sessions

#### Risk 4: Integration Issues
**Probability:** Medium  
**Impact:** Medium  
**Mitigation:**
- Continuous integration from start
- Integration tests early
- Regular integration testing
- Clear API contracts

#### Risk 5: Technical Debt Accumulation
**Probability:** High  
**Impact:** Medium  
**Mitigation:**
- Track technical debt explicitly
- Allocate time for debt remediation (20% of sprint)
- Prioritize high-impact debt
- No new features until critical debt addressed

#### Risk 6: Performance Issues
**Probability:** Medium  
**Impact:** Medium  
**Mitigation:**
- Performance testing during development
- Code profiling for hot paths
- Database query optimization
- Performance budgets defined

#### Risk 7: Security Vulnerabilities
**Probability:** Medium  
**Impact:** Critical  
**Mitigation:**
- Security code reviews for sensitive code
- Automated security scanning
- Dependency vulnerability scanning
- Follow secure coding practices

#### Risk 8: Developer Unavailability
**Probability:** Medium  
**Impact:** Medium  
**Mitigation:**
- Cross-training team members
- Documentation of work in progress
- Pair programming knowledge sharing
- Backup resources identified

## 15. Phase Transition

### Transition to Phase 4: Testing

#### Pre-Transition Activities
1. Code freeze
2. Generate final build
3. Deploy to test environment
4. Complete all documentation
5. Create testing handover package
6. Conduct Phase 3 retrospective

#### Handover to Phase 4
**From:** Development Team  
**To:** QA/Test Engineering Team

**Handover Package:**
- Application deployed in test environment
- Build/deployment artifacts
- Test data and seeding scripts
- Known issues list
- User acceptance test scenarios
- API documentation
- Test account credentials
- Environment configuration guide

**Handover Meeting Agenda:**
1. Application walkthrough (30 min)
2. Known issues review (15 min)
3. Test environment access (10 min)
4. Q&A (15 min)

### Rollback Procedures

If critical issues discovered:
1. Document issues
2. Assess impact
3. If show-stopper: return to development
4. Fix issues
5. Re-test
6. Re-attempt transition

## 18. Common Pitfalls

### Pitfall 1: Skipping Tests to Save Time
**Impact:** Technical debt, bugs in production  
**Prevention:** Enforce test coverage gates, TDD practices  
**Recovery:** Stop feature development, write missing tests

### Pitfall 2: Inadequate Code Reviews
**Impact:** Poor code quality, bugs, security issues  
**Prevention:** 100% review coverage, review checklists  
**Recovery:** Retroactive code reviews, refactoring sprints

### Pitfall 3: Ignoring Technical Debt
**Impact:** Slower development, quality degradation  
**Prevention:** Track debt, allocate remediation time  
**Recovery:** Dedicated debt reduction sprint

### Pitfall 4: Poor Communication
**Impact:** Integration issues, duplicated work  
**Prevention:** Daily standups, clear documentation  
**Recovery:** Team sync meetings, clarify responsibilities

### Pitfall 5: Gold Plating
**Impact:** Scope creep, timeline delays  
**Prevention:** Strict adherence to requirements  
**Recovery:** Remove unnecessary features

---

## 19. Best Practices

### Coding Practices
1. Follow SOLID principles
2. Keep functions small and focused
3. Use meaningful names
4. Comment complex logic
5. Avoid premature optimization
6. Refactor continuously
7. Use design patterns appropriately

### Testing Practices
1. Write tests first (TDD) or alongside code
2. Test behavior, not implementation
3. Use meaningful test names
4. Arrange-Act-Assert pattern
5. Mock external dependencies
6. Test edge cases
7. Keep tests fast

### Code Review Practices
1. Review promptly (<24 hours)
2. Be constructive and respectful
3. Use review checklists
4. Test the code locally
5. Check for security issues
6. Verify tests exist and pass
7. Approve only production-ready code

### Version Control Practices
1. Commit frequently
2. Write clear commit messages
3. Use feature branches
4. Keep main/master stable
5. Rebase/merge appropriately
6. Tag releases
7. Use pull requests for all changes

### CI/CD Practices
1. Run tests on every commit
2. Fail fast on errors
3. Keep builds fast
4. Monitor build health
5. Auto-generate artifacts
6. Use infrastructure as code
7. Maintain pipeline documentation
